title: Visual and Auditory Aesthetic Preferences Across Cultures
authors: Harin Lee, Eline Van Geert, Elif Celen, Raja Marjieh, Pol van Rijn, Minsu Park, Nori Jacoby
abstract: Research on how humans perceive aesthetics in shapes, colours, and music has predominantly focused on Western populations, limiting our understanding of how cultural environments shape aesthetic preferences. We present a large-scale cross-cultural study examining aesthetic preferences across five distinct modalities extensively explored in the literature: shape, curvature, colour, musical harmony and melody. We gather 401,403 preference judgements from 4,835 participants across 10 countries, systematically sampling two-dimensional parameter spaces for each modality. The findings reveal both universal patterns and cultural variations. Preferences for shape and curvature cross-culturally demonstrate a consistent preference for symmetrical forms. While colour preferences are categorically consistent, ratio-like preferences vary across cultures. Musical harmony shows strong agreement in interval relationships despite differing regions of preference within the broad frequency spectrum, while melody shows the highest cross-cultural variation. These results suggest that aesthetic preferences emerge from an interplay between shared perceptual mechanisms and cultural learning.
zh_title: 跨文化视角下的视觉与听觉审美偏好
zh_abstract: 关于人类如何感知形状、颜色与音乐之美的研究，历来主要聚焦西方人群，这限制了我们对文化环境如何塑造审美偏好的理解。本文报告一项大规模跨文化研究，考察文献中被广泛探讨的五种不同模态上的审美偏好：形状、曲率、颜色、音乐和声与旋律。我们在 10 个国家收集了 4,835 名参与者的 401,403 次偏好判断，并对每种模态的两个维度参数空间做系统采样。研究结果既揭示出普遍模式，也揭示出文化变异。形状与曲率上的偏好在跨文化层面表现出对对称形态的一贯偏好；颜色偏好在类别层面一致，但类比值层面的偏好则因文化而异。音乐和声在音程关系上表现出高度一致，尽管在宽频谱上偏好的区域有所不同；旋律则呈现出最高的跨文化变异。这些结果表明，审美偏好源自共享知觉机制与文化学习之间的交互作用。
citation: [101] Cross-Cultural Lab. Visual and auditory aesthetic preferences across cultures[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.14439, 2025. [arXiv]
